Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.vpn

Class VpnBackend

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.vpn.VpnBackend
public final class VpnBackend extends Object
The AWT-free VPN seam. The desktop ships no tunnel stack of its own, so - exactly like the Security Center handing scanning to ClamAV and the recorder handing capture to ffmpeg - this backend honestly delegates the tunnel to an installed tool. It resolves which tool to drive (nmcli for NetworkManager-managed connections, preferred because it already holds the credentials and integrates with the desktop; openvpn / wg-quick for a config file the user imported), builds the precise command lines, and parses their terse output into VpnProfile / VpnStatus values.

Every method here is pure and side-effect free - no process is started - so the whole command / parser table is unit-testable headless against recorded nmcli output. The thin, guarded ProcessBuilder launch lives in VpnPanel and is only ever reached from a user action. A missing tool, or a connect that needs privilege the session does not have, is surfaced by the panel as honest guidance, never as a fake "connected".

    • KNOWN_BACKENDS

      public static final List<String> KNOWN_BACKENDS
      Tunnel tools this backend knows how to drive, in preference order. nmcli leads (it reuses NetworkManager's stored VPN connections and secrets and needs no separate config); openvpn and wg-quick are the standalone fallbacks for an imported config file.

    • connectCommand

      public static List<String> connectCommand(String backend, VpnProfile profile)
      Builds the connect command for a profile under the given backend.
      • nmcli: nmcli connection up uuid <uuid> (or by name when there is no UUID);
      • openvpn: openvpn --config <path> --daemon (needs privilege, which the panel surfaces);
      • wg-quick: wg-quick up <name> (needs privilege).
      Parameters:
      backend - the tool to drive
      profile - the profile to connect
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when a required input is missing

    • disconnectCommand

      public static List<String> disconnectCommand(String backend, VpnProfile profile)
      Builds the disconnect command for a profile under the given backend. A standalone openvpn tunnel has no clean CLI teardown (it is a process), so this returns an empty list and the panel stops the tracked process instead.
      Parameters:
      backend - the tool driving the tunnel
      profile - the profile to disconnect
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when there is nothing to run

    • parseConnections

      public static List<VpnProfile> parseConnections(List<String> lines)
      Parses nmcli -t -f NAME,UUID,TYPE connection show output into the VPN profiles it contains, skipping non-VPN connections (ethernet, wi-fi, bridges). Terse fields escape a literal colon as \\:, so the split respects backslash escapes.
      Parameters:
      lines - the terse output (may be null)
      Returns:
      the VPN profiles, never null

    • parseStatus

      public static VpnStatus parseStatus(List<String> lines)
      Parses nmcli -t -f NAME,TYPE,DEVICE connection show --active output into a VpnStatus. The first active VPN-typed connection wins; when none is active the status is disconnected.
      Parameters:
      lines - the terse output (may be null)
      Returns:
      the status, never null
